stem:
Bina chews plain boiled rice for about one minute and compares it with unchewed boiled rice using iodine. She also has egg white as a protein food that is not starch. Iodine can give a blue-black colour with starch, and chewed rice may taste sweet when sugar forms.

Which observation best supports that saliva breaks starch into sugar?

options.text: Unchewed boiled rice also gives little or no blue-black colour with iodine.
The chewed boiled rice shows little or no blue-black colour with iodine.
Saliva changes sugar into starch, so iodine turns darker after chewing.
Saliva changes the protein in egg white into sugar.

teacher.key_rationale: Weaker iodine colour after chewing shows some starch has changed into sugar. The unchewed control should still stain; saliva does not make starch from sugar or turn egg-white protein into sugar.
